name: Mahabalipuram
description: UNESCO-recognized coastal heritage town known for ancient rock-cut temples and shore monuments from the Pallava period.
quickNotes: Best known for Shore Temple and Pancha Rathas.
Ideal for compact 60-90 minute heritage walk.
Popular sunrise and seaside photography stop.
UNESCO-listed monuments are within short drive distance.
Stone-carving craft shops are common around the site.
Morning visits are generally less crowded.

name: Dakshina Chitra
description: Living-history museum showcasing South Indian arts, architecture, and traditional crafts through curated exhibits.
quickNotes: Open-air cultural museum with recreated heritage homes.
Handicraft demonstrations and folk-art exhibits available.
Great spot for short curated cultural immersion.
Traditional architecture sections represent multiple South Indian states.
Workshops and performances are often scheduled on weekends.
Pathways are easy to cover in a compact visit window.

name: St. Thomas Mount
description: Historic hilltop church site offering panoramic city views and significant religious heritage.
quickNotes: Hilltop location with broad view of Chennai skyline.
Historic chapel with strong religious significance.
Quick evening stop recommended for view and photos.
Access includes steps and a short uphill approach.
Clear weather offers excellent citywide visibility.
Useful stop for both heritage and viewpoint interests.

name: Marina Beach
description: Iconic urban beachfront in Chennai known for its long sandy shoreline, sunrise views, and lively promenade.
quickNotes: One of the longest urban beaches in the world.
Sunrise and sunset are ideal times for photography.
A lively stretch with popular local snack stalls.
Close to major city landmarks and memorials.
Great for short walks along the broad sandy shore.
Evenings are vibrant with family-friendly activity zones.
Follow local safety advisories and avoid rough surf areas.

name: Egmore Museum
description: Government Museum complex with archaeology, art, and historical galleries representing Tamil Nadu's legacy.
quickNotes: One of India's oldest museums with diverse collections.
Highlights include archaeology, art, and bronze galleries.
Compact heritage stop in central Chennai.
Complex includes multiple buildings with distinct exhibits.
Bronze and numismatic sections are visitor favorites.
Centrally located with convenient city access.

name: Valluvar Kottam
description: Monument dedicated to Tamil poet Thiruvalluvar, featuring a large stone chariot and an auditorium of carved verses.
quickNotes: Landmark cultural monument in central Chennai.
Known for the giant temple-chariot style structure.
Ideal for a short heritage and architecture stop.
Easily accessible from major city routes.

name: Santhome Church
description: Historic basilica built over the traditional tomb site of St. Thomas, known for neo-gothic architecture.
quickNotes: One of the major Christian heritage sites in Chennai.
Distinct white neo-gothic facade and serene interiors.
Suitable for a calm cultural and spiritual visit.
Located close to Marina and other city landmarks.

name: Kapaleeswarar Temple
description: Renowned Dravidian-style temple in Mylapore dedicated to Lord Shiva, famous for its colorful gopuram.
quickNotes: Iconic Mylapore temple with intricate tower sculptures.
Active worship site with traditional South Indian rituals.
Best visited in early morning or evening hours.
Surrounded by vibrant local streets and shops.
